extra.message: convertTicketBundleToFormat builds a shell command by interpolating the caller-supplied exportFormat query parameter (via outputPath) into `pandoc ${sourcePath} -o ${outputPath}` and executes it with spawn('bash', ['-c', cmd], { shell: true }). Unlike convertEscalationBundleToFormat, which allowlists formats (ALLOWED_ESCALATION_REPORT_FORMATS) and spawns with shell: false, exportFormat here is never validated, allowing command injection (e.g. exportFormat=`x; rm -rf /` or command substitution).

exportTicketsBundle inserts the caller-supplied reportLabel query parameter directly into a Content-Disposition header without stripping CR/LF, enabling HTTP response header injection (CRLF injection). The parallel exportEscalationsBundle endpoint sanitizes its label with rawLabel.replace(/[\r\n]/g, '') (line 150), but this endpoint does not.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: renderCategoryReport concatenates the user-controlled ticket category (set via CreateTicketDto.category with no format validation) into path.join(this.templatesDir, `${category}.txt`) and reads it with fs.readFileSync with no path validation. A ticket whose category contains ../ sequences traverses outside the templates directory (arbitrary file read). renderQueueReport (line 65) guards against this with a startsWith check, but this method omits it.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: saveBrandingAsset writes the uploaded file to path.join(brandingDir, file.originalname) using the attacker-controlled original filename with no sanitization. A crafted originalname (e.g. ../../../../etc/cron.d/x) writes arbitrary files outside the branding directory. saveWorkspaceIconAsset correctly uses a generated filename instead of file.originalname.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: findStaffRecordByEmail builds an LDAP filter directly from the caller-supplied email query parameter: `(mail=${email})` without escaping. An attacker can inject LDAP metacharacters (e.g. * ( ) \) to alter the filter. The escapeLdapFilterValue helper exists and is used by searchStaffDirectory and syncStaffRoleFromDirectory, but is not applied here.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: findById returns the full escalation (including ticket, requester and assignee emails) to any caller who passes membershipTier=partner_reviewer as a query parameter, completely bypassing the organization/role access check that follows. Any authenticated user (including customer_user) can read any escalation's sensitive data by setting this query parameter.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: admitPartnerHandoff verifies the partner handoff token with algorithms: ['HS256', 'none'], permitting the unsecured 'none' algorithm, and falls back to jwt.decode(handoffToken) (no signature verification) whenever verification fails. A caller can forge a handoff context. The signing secret also defaults to an empty string when PARTNER_HANDOFF_SECRET is unset.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: getCapacityForecast returns the raw error message and stack trace to the caller whenever the x-ops-context header is set to 'internal-ops'. This header is fully caller-controlled (any team_lead/admin), so an attacker can trigger an error and receive internal exception details and stack traces (information disclosure). getBreachSummary correctly logs detail server-side and returns only a generic message.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: forgotPassword returns the generated resetToken in the HTTP response body. The endpoint is unauthenticated, so an attacker can request a reset for any victim's email and receive the token, then call reset-password to take over the account. The token should only be delivered out-of-band (email), never returned to the requester.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: initializeAccount (an unauthenticated endpoint) lets the caller control the bcrypt cost factor via dto.provisioningTier, so a caller can submit provisioningTier: 4 (or 1) and have their password stored with an extremely weak hash, defeating the intended saltRounds=12. The cost factor should be fixed server-side and never attacker-controlled.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The JWT strategy falls back to a hardcoded secret 'change-me-in-production-use-a-real-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is not set, allowing anyone to forge valid auth tokens in a misconfigured deployment. portal.service.ts (line 57) has a similar fallback secret 'portal-dev-secret'.

Seed script provisions known admin/lead/agent accounts with hardcoded, predictable passwords (Admin123!, Lead123!, Agent123!) that grant elevated roles if the seed is run against a shared environment.

The portal checkin endpoint sets the portal_session cookie (which holds a session token) with res.cookie('portal_session', result.cookieValue) and no options, so it lacks HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags. The workspace-context cookie in the same controller sets httpOnly/secure/sameSite. A session cookie without HttpOnly is exposed to XSS-based token theft.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
